determinism.canonicalization: strict duplicate-rejecting sorted compact ASCII JSON with one LF, NFC strings, bounded integers, full lowercase SHA-256 identities, no floats, and exact array order
determinism.classification: one closed precedence table maps worker status, Evidence status, Certificate verdict, checker agreement, and accepted planner outcomes without exception-dependent or text-dependent fallback
determinism.graph: strategy traversal starts at the exact entry and uses only content-addressed planner transitions; plan order breaks no runtime race because v1 launches sequentially
determinism.identity: every nested identity hashes its complete canonical preimage with only its own digest field null; the final identity binds exact semantic metadata and byte digests
determinism.platform: worker platform capability can affect an explicit unsupported outcome but path spelling, PID, handles, exit encoding, scheduling, and runtime measurements do not alter semantic classification
determinism.preference: planner_order_no_sound_witness_declaration is the only accepted policy until a superseding capability contract exposes a sound counterexample-path declaration
determinism.replay: identical canonical inputs and identical isolated producer and checker semantic bytes reproduce the same attempts, inconclusive records, transition path, verdict, selected identities, and result bytes across Python 3.10 through 3.14 and Linux, macOS, and Windows

effects.cache: none; MH-053 retains no outcome beyond returned immutable values and MH-055 owns all reusable content-addressed caching
effects.clock: no portfolio clock; relative enforcement and nonsemantic observations remain wholly inside the accepted isolated-worker supervisor
effects.environment: no environment read; only the supervisor creates its fixed minimal child environment and executable paths are explicit noncanonical effect inputs
effects.filesystem: the portfolio itself reads no path and writes nothing; the supervisor alone validates executables and owns its private workspace directories
effects.memory: bounded in-memory canonical parsing and immutable metadata only; producer and checker memory is hard-bounded by separate isolated-worker invocations
effects.mutation: caller inputs are never mutated or retained through mutable aliases; ledger evolution is replacement by exact returned canonical bytes
effects.network: none in orchestration; a producer or checker effect is possible only through an accepted declared plugin and isolated worker and never grants authority
effects.persistence: none; MH-054 owns durable audit and replay event storage
effects.process: only indirect calls to supervise_worker; no subprocess, multiprocessing, shell, dynamic entry point, plugin import, or process API is used by the portfolio
effects.solver: only isolated untrusted producer or exact checker work; the portfolio never calls or interprets a solver directly

ensures: run_portfolio is total over ordinary malformed, stale, unavailable, unsupported, exhausted, cancelled, producer-failed, checker-failed, and disagreement inputs and returns one closed immutable ProofSearchPortfolioResult without converting an exception or partial artifact into success.

Before launch the portfolio strictly parses and recomputes the request, plan, descriptor, execution-binding, artifact, parent-ledger, component, evidence-expectation, executable, protocol, and complete graph identities; any missing, duplicate, stale, cross-plan, or surplus binding returns invalid without launching work.

The portfolio begins only at the exact plan entry, executes at most one producer and one checker for each visited strategy, follows the exact accepted transition for the classified outcome, never visits a strategy twice, and never schedules an unreachable, hidden, speculative, retry, or timing-selected node.

Every producer and checker invocation is constructed inside the portfolio as one canonical MH-C-ISOLATED-WORKER-001 request and is executed only by supervise_worker with a unique deterministic lease and child-budget identity; no callable, live plugin, caller-authored worker result, in-process solver, or direct subprocess path exists.

The exact parent ledger returned by each reconciled worker becomes the byte-for-byte input ledger for the next invocation. A missing reconciliation, invalid returned ledger, reused lease, insufficient capacity, unsupported containment, cleanup failure, or any resource exhaustion prevents checked promotion.

A completed producer stdout is accepted as a candidate only when it is canonical mathhead.evidence.v1, has status produced, binds the exact obligation subject, producer component, expected evidence format, accepted Evidence contract, and one explicit org.mathhead.portfolio.claim equal to proved or refuted; all other producer bytes classify as invalid evidence or the exact non-success outcome.

The checker executes in a separate isolated invocation with the exact Evidence bytes appended through the closed canonical_evidence_certificate_v1 protocol and returns one canonical portfolio checker decision plus canonical Certificate bytes bound by exact length and digest.

Checked promotion requires the exact planned checker component, the same strategy, subject, Evidence bytes and claim, a canonical Certificate whose subject and Evidence reference agree, a verified verdict with checker_attested or external_verified authority, and a checker decision that independently agrees on proved or refuted.

Checker rejection, unsupported output, incomplete replay, invalid Certificate, disagreement, timeout, exhaustion, cancellation, crash, protocol failure, or cleanup failure stays explicit, carries no selected evidence or certificate, and follows only the accepted planner transition.

Because accepted v1 capability descriptors contain no sound counterexample-path declaration, the portfolio preserves planner order and records planner_order_no_sound_witness_declaration; it never infers counterexample capability from names, descriptions, evidence payload text, prior runs, or mathematical folklore.

Within one accepted checked decision, refuted is retained as an exact checked counterexample verdict and is never weakened to a proof or inconclusive label; absence of a witness, exhausted enumeration, successful process exit, repeated bytes, or producer majority cannot establish proved.

Every nonterminal fallback produces one immutable PortfolioInconclusive record, and every visited strategy produces one immutable PortfolioAttempt binding producer and checker results, selected transition, before and after ledger identities, evidence and decision identities, and plan order.

The final result separates execution status, mathematical_verdict, reason, selected strategy and artifacts, authority tier, attempts, inconclusive outcomes, and final budget. The portfolio value itself always has mathematical_authority false and cannot substitute for the selected Certificate or its independent checker.

Canonical result identity binds all semantic inputs, attempt order, classifications, transitions, selected artifacts, authority tier, and final ledger while excluding executable and workspace paths, PID, handles, temporary names, scheduling, arrival timing, raw monotonic samples, platform exit spelling, and clock origins.

All seven public value classes are closed final immutable values; direct construction, subclassing, mutation, alias mutation, dataclass replacement, pickling, noncanonical parsing, copied status fields, or repaired hashes cannot create a valid request, binding, decision, attempt, inconclusive record, or result.

MemoryError, KeyboardInterrupt, and SystemExit propagate only after the active supervisor has applied its cleanup behavior; no ordinary result converts these conditions into success, checked evidence, checker agreement, or authority.

epistemics.checked_promotion: a selected proved or refuted verdict records exact agreement between canonical Evidence and a separately executed exact planned checker Certificate; the portfolio result itself remains non-authoritative
epistemics.counterexample: refuted means an exact independently checked counterexample claim; it is preferred only where an accepted capability declaration soundly permits reordering, which v1 does not yet expose
epistemics.inconclusive: unsupported, producer error, ambiguity, truncation, checker inconclusive, checker disagreement, or invalid evidence is retained as negative execution knowledge and never rewritten as mathematical failure or truth
epistemics.mathematical_truth: never inferred from planning, ordering, process completion, budget use, deterministic bytes, search coverage, absence of a witness, producer consensus, or portfolio metadata
epistemics.producer: canonical Evidence from a completed isolated producer remains a producer report and cannot select a proved or refuted verdict without the exact independent checker path
epistemics.resource_outcome: exhaustion and cancellation describe bounded execution only and cannot prove, refute, weaken, strengthen, or complete a mathematical claim
epistemics.verifier_failure: checker or verification failure is terminal under the accepted planner and cannot fall back, promote partial artifacts, or borrow producer authority

invariants: The six normative schemas are exact, closed, content-addressed, compiled into production, and independently rebound before any request, binding, nested value, or result is accepted.

Request, descriptor, binding, artifact, executable, plan, strategy, component, evidence expectation, parent ledger, and every returned worker result are selected only by exact byte identities; names and prose never repair or substitute identity.

There is exactly one execution binding and one executable-path pair per planned strategy in plan order, and every binding artifact is a member of the request's complete artifact inventory with no duplicate role or digest-length ambiguity.

Each visited strategy launches its producer at most once and, only after valid produced Evidence, its checker at most once; the portfolio has no retry, speculation, concurrent race, hidden fallback, dynamic import, in-process execution, or direct process escape hatch.

Producer and checker leases and child IDs are deterministic, unique across the request, bound to phase and strategy order, reserved before launch, closed by the supervisor, reconciled exactly once, and never reused after any outcome.

The next invocation receives exactly the previous reconciled parent ledger bytes; no usage is hidden, double charged, silently refunded, clamped, inferred from exit status, or accepted from caller-authored accounting.

A worker result with tree_terminated false, lease_reconciled false, missing parent bytes, omitted output, unsupported containment, non-completed status, or invalid full identity cannot contribute Evidence, Certificate, agreement, or success.

Evidence must be exact canonical produced Evidence for the planned subject, component and expected format and must declare exactly one proved or refuted portfolio claim; payload contents, diagnostic prose, filenames, or process output outside that object cannot classify a claim.

Certificate and checker decision must bind the same exact Evidence bytes, subject, strategy, producer, checker, claim, verdict, authority and accepted contracts; verified status without agreement, independent component separation, and complete digest binding is invalid.

No producer may act as its own checker, no checker may be substituted by executable name or caller assertion, and multiple producer reports or repeated runs cannot emulate independent checker agreement.
The accepted planner transition for the exact classified outcome is the sole source of the next node or terminal state; verifier failure, exhaustion and cancellation always stop exactly as planned.

Every non-success fallback is represented once in attempts and once in inconclusive outcomes in the same order; a selected checked verdict has exactly one strategy, Evidence, Certificate, decision, authority tier, and final reconciled ledger.

The preference policy cannot reorder v1 strategies because no sound witness-path declaration exists; any future counterexample-first reordering requires a superseding contract and capability schema rather than heuristic inference.

No canonical value contains executable or workspace paths, environment content, secrets, callables, modules, plugin instances, processes, PIDs, raw handles, clock origins, temporary names, mutable aliases, or retained cancellation objects.

Any repaired hash, copied verified field, changed claim, swapped component, stale context, changed artifact, invalid ledger, unknown outcome, duplicate key, float, bool-as-int, non-NFC string, over-limit value, or incomplete cleanup invalidates or downgrades the result without authority.
raises: ProofSearchPortfolioValidationError with kind type, encoding, json, duplicate, schema, canonical, identity, contract, request, plan, descriptor, binding, artifact, budget, executable, evidence, certificate, checker, transition, result, or limit is raised only by explicitly requested strict constructors, parsers, serializers, validators, accessors, and unrecoverable pre-launch API misuse.

Ordinary malformed, stale, missing, surplus, unavailable, unsupported, exhausted, cancelled, failed, truncated, ambiguous, checker-inconclusive, checker-disagreement, verifier-failed, or invalid-evidence cases return their exact closed non-authoritative result.
PermissionError is raised for direct public construction; TypeError is raised for subclass and pickle attempts; safe copy preserves immutable identity or fails.
MemoryError, KeyboardInterrupt, and SystemExit propagate unchanged after isolated-worker cleanup and cannot become a portfolio result.
requires: MH-C-WORKFLOW-001=99cfdf17371938af65c4203c02cbaac0bf73470e9fab59f7a6d62360fc0b7cca governs this critical orchestration and checked-promotion boundary.

request, planning_result, and parent_budget are exact built-in bytes; descriptors, bindings, and artifacts are exact built-in tuples of exact built-in bytes; executable_paths is an exact built-in tuple of two-string exact built-in tuples; workspace_root is an exact built-in string; cancel_event is None or one exact threading.Event.

request is canonical mathhead.proof-search-portfolio-request.v1 and binds the exact planning result, open parent ledger, complete sorted descriptor inventory, exact plan-order execution-binding inventory, complete ordered artifact inventory, and planner_order_no_sound_witness_declaration preference policy.

planning_result is one canonical valid planned MH-C-DETERMINISTIC-PLANNER-001 result with a finite reachable acyclic strategy graph, complete ordered outcomes, exact evidence expectations, and no partial or repaired identity.

parent_budget is one canonical independently valid open MH-C-RESOURCE-BUDGET-001 ledger whose byte identity equals the request and whose accepted limits and history have no terminal event or reused portfolio lease identity.

Every planned strategy has exactly one canonical execution binding in plan order; its descriptor, components, families, direct producer and checker argument vectors, executable digests, artifact subset, and protocol match the exact accepted plan and descriptor bytes.

Every input artifact has one unique role and exact positive or zero byte length and SHA-256 binding; no path, stream, iterator, mutable buffer, alias, omitted, duplicate, or surplus artifact is accepted.

Each executable path is absolute and is validated by MH-C-ISOLATED-WORKER-001 against the bound producer or checker executable digest; workspace_root satisfies that supervisor contract without becoming canonical result data.
